title: Project render fails with "Directory not empty (os error 39)" removing execute-results when the project is on NFS
description:
### Bug description

Rendering a knitr document inside a Quarto project that lives on an NFS mount fails intermittently, after all code has executed and before pandoc runs:

```
processing file: analysis.qmd
output file: analysis.knit.md

ERROR: Directory not empty (os error 39): remove '/nfs/project/analyses/analysis_files/execute-results'

Stack trace:
    at Object.removeSync (ext:deno_fs/30_fs.js:250:3)
    at safeRemoveSync (file:///usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/quarto/bin/quarto.js:3228:10)
    at removeIfExists (file:///usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/quarto/bin/quarto.js:7970:5)
    at removeFreezeResults (file:///usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/quarto/bin/quarto.js:136700:3)
    at renderExecute (file:///usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/quarto/bin/quarto.js:136863:5)
    at async renderFileInternal (file:///usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/quarto/bin/quarto.js:137094:35)
    at async renderFiles (file:///usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/quarto/bin/quarto.js:136884:9)
    at async renderProject (file:///usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/quarto/bin/quarto.js:137468:23)
```

Immediately afterwards, `ls -la analysis_files/execute-results/` shows the directory is empty.

### What seems to happen

In a project render, `renderExecute()` (`src/command/render/render-files.ts`) writes the freeze result `<doc>_files/execute-results/html.json`, copies it to the freezer, and then calls `removeFreezeResults()`, which removes `execute-results` right away (the project does not use `freeze`). On NFS, unlinking a file whose handle has not fully closed triggers the client's "silly rename": the file becomes a hidden `.nfsXXXX` placeholder until the last handle closes. The directory is therefore briefly non-empty, `removeSync` fails with ENOTEMPTY, and the render aborts. By the time a user inspects the directory, the placeholder is gone.

This fits the observations:

- It happens after all code has run, so every chunk's side effects (saved files, figures) exist, but no HTML is written.
- It is intermittent. The same document sometimes renders cleanly, and long documents with large output seem more affected.
- It never happens with the same files on local disk.
- It never happens outside a project (single-file renders take a different path that skips the freeze write).

### Reproduction

1. A Quarto project (`_quarto.yml` with `project: type: default`) on an NFS-mounted directory.
2. A knitr `.qmd` with substantial printed output and a figure.
3. `quarto render path/to/doc.qmd` repeatedly; some runs fail as above.

We cannot share our documents (clinical data), and the failure depends on NFS timing, so a minimal example on local disk will not reproduce it.

### Workaround

Make `execute-results` a symlink to a directory on local disk before rendering:

```bash
files_dir="doc_files"
local_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
rm -rf "$files_dir" && mkdir -p "$files_dir"
ln -s "$local_dir" "$files_dir/execute-results"
quarto render doc.qmd
```

Quarto writes `html.json` through the link and, on cleanup, removes the link itself, so nothing is unlinked on NFS. The render then succeeds, with project mode and pre/post-render scripts intact. (Symlinking the whole `_files` directory instead does not work: the final cleanup refuses to remove a directory that resolves outside the project.)

### Possible fixes

- Retry the removal of `execute-results` on ENOTEMPTY/EBUSY with a short backoff, as many tools do for NFS.
- Treat failure to remove `execute-results` as a warning rather than a fatal error, since the freeze result has already been copied to the freezer.
- When freeze is not enabled, skip writing `execute-results/html.json` beside the document at all.

### Environment

- Quarto 1.10.18 (bundled with Posit Workbench)
- R 4.6.1, knitr 1.51, rmarkdown 2.31
- RHEL 8.10, project directory on an NFS mount

### Related

#2380 also concerns projects on network storage, but it is a Windows UNC path-resolution failure (`os error 3`); this is a Linux NFS delete race (`os error 39`).

title: Tracking issue: Quarto projects on network and cloud-synced file systems
description:
We have many reports about Quarto failing when a project lives on a network drive (SMB, NFS, CIFS, UNC path) or a cloud-synced folder (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive). They look similar from the outside but fail at different places for different reasons. This issue groups them by root cause, so we know which fix covers which report.

Our general recommendation is still to work on a local file system. Some of these failures are in our code and fixable though.

All open issues below are attached as sub-issues of this one.

## Transient removal failures during render

Quarto removes a directory it just wrote, in one attempt, and fails the render on any error.

- #15071: summary and possible directions
- #15054, #8972, #7993, #6616, #4614 (closed)

## UNC paths

Paths like `\\server\share\project` not resolving (`os error 3` on `stat 'UNC\...'`). Mapping the share to a drive letter works around it.

- #2380, #1774, #758, #2711 (closed)

## Project cache on network mounts (Deno KV / SQLite locking)

`database is locked` when opening the project cache on CIFS or NFS mounts. SQLite locking is not reliable on network file systems ([SQLite FAQ](https://www.sqlite.org/faq.html#q5)). This needs the cache to live elsewhere or an opt-out, not a retry.

- #13006, Discussion #14568

## Cloud sync clients racing with other file operations

Sync clients locking or changing files while Quarto writes, copies or walks them (`mkdir`, directory walk, `site_libs` copies).

- #4670, #2174, #3871, #8457, #8239
- #6895: detect and warn when the project is in a synced folder

## Deno permissions on network drives (fixed)

- #11332, fixed by #11385

title: Render fails when removing a temporary directory hits a transient lock or network file system error
description:
During render, Quarto removes several directories it has just written or copied. Each removal is a single `Deno.removeSync(path, { recursive: true })` attempt, and any error aborts the render. On network file systems, cloud-synced folders, or with another process scanning the folder (editor, antivirus, sync client), this removal can fail transiently even though the directory is empty a moment later.

This happens after all code has executed, so the user loses the whole render for a cleanup step.

## Reported cases

All with the same pattern: removal right after write or copy, one attempt, fatal error.

`execute-results` removal in project render (`removeFreezeResults`):

- #15054: Linux NFS, `Directory not empty (os error 39)`, Quarto 1.10.18
- #8972: Windows mapped network drive, `An unexpected network error occurred. (os error 59)`, Quarto 1.4.550
- #2380 (comment from 2023-07-02): Google Drive, `NotFound (os error 2)`
- Discussions #6143 and #10775

Render cleanup of `_files`, `libs` and `mediabag` (`renderCleanup`, `removeIfEmptyDir`):

- #7993: Google Drive, `os error 2` removing `_files\libs` with `embed-resources`
- #6616: Windows, `os error 303` then `os error 32` removing `mediabag`, also on local disk with an editor open on the project
- #4614 (closed by #7921)

## Code path

In a project render, the execute result is written beside the document, copied to the freezer, then removed:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/183154fa2c026b3f684d9985856a3d555f4f457e/src/command/render/render-files.ts#L242-L284

The removal goes through `safeRemoveSync`, which only ignores the error if the path is gone afterwards:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/183154fa2c026b3f684d9985856a3d555f4f457e/src/deno_ral/fs.ts#L114-L125

This was added for denoland/deno#18996 (removal succeeds but reports an error) and covers the Google Drive `os error 2` case when the directory ends up removed. It does not cover cases where the directory still exists at the time of the check: NFS `ENOTEMPTY`, SMB `os error 59`, sharing violations.

Render cleanup has the same pattern:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/183154fa2c026b3f684d9985856a3d555f4f457e/src/command/render/cleanup.ts#L92-L109

Deno does not retry either. `Deno.remove` calls Rust `std::fs::remove_dir_all`, which on Linux returns `ENOTEMPTY` from the final `rmdir` directly, and on Windows only retries a few times without waiting, for `ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION` (32) and `ERROR_DIR_NOT_EMPTY` (145).

## Why the directory is empty right after

On NFS, unlinking a file that still has an open handle on the client renames it to a hidden `.nfsXXXX` file until the last handle closes (see "silly rename" in the [Linux NFS FAQ](https://nfs.sourceforge.net/#faq_d2)). `rmdir` fails with `ENOTEMPTY` during that window. This matches what #15054 describes. On Windows, a sync client, antivirus, indexer or editor holding the file produces `os error 32` / `145` / `303` the same way.

From my reading of the code, Quarto does not hold a handle on these files at removal time (all writes and copies use sync APIs that close the file). So the holder is another process, and we can't control it.

## Prior work

- #1536 added `safeRemoveIfExists` (warn instead of fail). It is used for freezer pruning, with a comment about network drives, but not for `execute-results`:

  https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/183154fa2c026b3f684d9985856a3d555f4f457e/src/command/render/freeze.ts#L227-L243

- #7921 and #10377 introduced and extended `safeRemoveSync`.
- #10629 tried a retry loop on Windows. Measured on a local Windows mediabag lock: 74 to 300 attempts, 18 to 70 ms before success. Discussion there: we would prefer a pause-and-retry with a short timeout, and giving up silently on removal should not be the default. Closed unmerged.

## Possible directions

We could:

- Retry the removal with a short sleep, only after a failure, so there is no cost in the normal case. Node's `fs.rm` does this with `maxRetries` / `retryDelay` for `EBUSY`, `EMFILE`, `ENFILE`, `ENOTEMPTY` and `EPERM`; on Windows, 32, 145 and 303 would be the matching codes. `os error 59` is not in any established retry list.
- For `execute-results` specifically, report a warning instead of failing the render when the removal still fails, since the result is already in the freezer at this point. A leftover `execute-results` is not harmless (it could be picked on next thaw or end up in the output), so it should be cleaned up on the next execution.
- Write the execute result directly into the freezer instead of beside the document. This removes the write-then-remove step entirely, but changes how the freezer mirrors `<doc>_files`.

Testing will need a way to reproduce without a network share: holding a file handle from another process (Windows sharing violation) or a local NFS loopback mount on Linux.

title: Typst output keeps Markdown escapes in keywords and other metadata strings
description:
### I have:

- [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues
- [x] installed the latest version of [Quarto CLI](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/latest)
- [x] formatted my issue following the [Bug Reports guide](https://quarto.org/bug-reports.html)

### Bug description

In Typst output, keywords keep their Markdown escapes.
A keyword such as `snake_case` reaches the PDF metadata as `snake\_case`.

The backslash is stored in the PDF itself, in the Info dictionary (`/Keywords (snake\\_case, a\\*b)`) and in the XMP metadata (`<pdf:Keywords>snake\_case, a\*b</pdf:Keywords>`).
Readers see it in the Keywords field of the document properties in any PDF viewer, and tools that index PDF metadata pick it up too.
The page content is not affected, since the default template does not print keywords.

Only Typst is affected.
The same document gives `snake_case, a*b` in every other format that writes keywords:

- `html` and `revealjs`: `<meta name="keywords" content="snake_case, a*b">`.
- `pdf` (LaTeX): `pdfkeywords={\xmpquote{snake\_case}, \xmpquote{a*b}}`, which LaTeX turns into `snake_case, a*b` in the PDF.
- `docx`: `<cp:keywords>snake_case, a*b</cp:keywords>`.
- `odt`: `<meta:keyword>snake_case, a*b</meta:keyword>`.

The Typst partial puts the metadata inside a string, `keywords: ($for(keywords)$"$keywords$",$endfor$)`.
Pandoc renders the value as Typst markup first, so `_` becomes `\_` and `*` becomes `\*`.
Inside a Typst string, those backslashes are kept as they are.

Template partials in extensions hit the same thing with any path read from metadata, for example `image("$custom-logo$")`.
Here Typst stops with `error: path must not contain a backslash` when the path holds an underscore, such as `../_extensions/...`.

### Steps to reproduce

````qmd
---
title: "Keywords"
format:
  typst:
    keep-typ: true
keywords: [snake_case, "a*b"]
---

Text.
````

Render it, then look at `index.typ` and at the PDF metadata:

```bash
quarto render index.qmd
grep -n 'keywords: ("' index.typ
pdfinfo index.pdf | grep Keywords
```

### Actual behavior

```txt
keywords: ("snake\_case","a\*b",),
Keywords:        snake\_case, a\*b
```

### Expected behavior

```txt
keywords: ("snake_case","a*b",),
Keywords:        snake_case, a*b
```

### Your environment

- IDE: none, rendered from the command line.
- OS: macOS 27.0.

title: A `language` file set in a format extension is resolved against the wrong directory
description:
### I have

- [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues
- [x] installed the latest version of [Quarto CLI](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/latest)
- [x] formatted my issue following the [Bug Reports guide](https://quarto.org/bug-reports.html)

### Bug description

A format extension can't point `language` at a translation file of its own.
Quarto looks for the file in the wrong place and stops the render, so every document that uses the format fails.
It doesn't depend on the output format: `html`, `pdf`, `docx`, `typst`, and `revealjs` all fail the same way.
The same strings set inline under `language` in `_extension.yml` work, so only the file form is broken.

Two parts of Quarto prepare the path, and each one assumes a different base directory:

1. `resolveExtensionPaths` rewrites the paths in `_extension.yml` with `toInputRelativePaths`, so `_language.yml` becomes `_extensions/langfile/_language.yml`.
   That value is relative to the directory of the document.
2. `readExtensionFormat` then calls `resolveFormatsFromMetadata(extensionMetadata, extension.path, ...)`.
   That function takes `dirname(input)` as its base, and `extension.path` is already the extension directory, so the base ends up as the parent, `_extensions/`.
   `resolveLanguageMetadata` joins the two, which gives `_extensions/_extensions/langfile/_language.yml`.

- https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/b86f98d382940bef6c65f37ea0bdfba844f19b6d/src/extension/extension.ts#L457-L463
- https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/b86f98d382940bef6c65f37ea0bdfba844f19b6d/src/command/render/render-contexts.ts#L720-L724
- https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/b86f98d382940bef6c65f37ea0bdfba844f19b6d/src/command/render/render-contexts.ts#L100
- https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/b86f98d382940bef6c65f37ea0bdfba844f19b6d/src/core/language.ts#L148-L158

The extension can't work around this with another relative path.
Step 1 rewrites any path that exists, `../_language.yml` included, and step 2 then joins it to `_extensions/` all the same.

This matters more now that `$quarto.language.*$` exposes these strings to templates, and that custom keys reach them (#14772).
A format extension would naturally keep its own strings in a `_language.yml` with per-language files beside it, the same way Quarto ships its translations.
At the moment the only option is to inline them under `language` in `_extension.yml`.

### Steps to reproduce

Three files.

`_extensions/langfile/_extension.yml`:

```yaml
title: Language file
author: Example
version: 1.0.0
contributes:
  formats:
    html:
      language: _language.yml
```

`_extensions/langfile/_language.yml`:

```yaml
toc-title-document: "Contents from the extension"
```

`index.qmd`:

````qmd
---
title: "Language file shipped by an extension"
format: langfile-html
toc: true
---

## Section

Body.
````

Then:

```sh
quarto render index.qmd
```

### Actual behavior

The render stops before Pandoc runs:

```text
ERROR: Specified 'language' file does not exist: /path/to/project/_extensions/_extensions/langfile/_language.yml

Stack trace:
    at resolveLanguageMetadata (file:///path/to/quarto-cli/src/core/language.ts:152:13)
    at resolveFormatsFromMetadata (file:///path/to/quarto-cli/src/command/render/render-contexts.ts:116:9)
    at async readExtensionFormat (file:///path/to/quarto-cli/src/command/render/render-contexts.ts:720:23)
    at async resolveFormats (file:///path/to/quarto-cli/src/command/render/render-contexts.ts:544:31)
    at async renderContexts (file:///path/to/quarto-cli/src/command/render/render-contexts.ts:230:19)
    at async renderFileInternal (file:///path/to/quarto-cli/src/command/render/render-files.ts:448:16)
```

I get this error on a dev build of `main` at b86f98d382940bef6c65f37ea0bdfba844f19b6d, and the same one on 1.10.19, with each of these:

- `html`, `pdf`, `docx`, `typst`, and `revealjs` as the base format of the extension.
- An extension under an organisation directory inside a project (`_extensions/acme/langfile/`), where the path becomes `_extensions/acme/_extensions/acme/langfile/_language.yml`.

Setting `toc-title-document` inline under `language` in `_extension.yml` instead works on both versions, and the title reads "Contents from the extension".

### Expected behavior

Quarto should resolve the file relative to the extension directory, as it does for `template-partials` and the other paths in `_extension.yml`.
The render should then succeed and the table of contents should read "Contents from the extension".

Per-language files beside it (`_language-fr.yml`) should load the same way they do for a document or project `language` file.

title: Listing categories cannot be reached or used with a keyboard
description:
### I have: - [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues - [x] installed the latest version of [Quarto CLI](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/latest) - [x] formatted my issue following the [Bug Reports guide](https://quarto.org/bug-reports.html) ### Bug description Listing categories can only be used with a mouse. The category tags on each listing item, in the default and grid listing types, are `

None of them has a `role`, a `tabindex` or a key handler, so Tab never reaches them, and screen readers do not present them as controls. title: a11y: `kbd` shortcode screen-reader text is missing, wrong, or read out of order
description: ## I have: - [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues - [x] installed the latest version of [Quarto CLI](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/latest) - [x] formatted my issue following the [Bug Reports guide](https://quarto.org/bug-reports.html) ## Bug description In HTML, the `kbd` shortcode hides the visible `` with `aria-hidden="true"`. It puts the screen-reader text in a `span.visually-hidden` after it. This span has three problems: | Shortcode | WCAG | What is wrong | |---|---|---| | OS arguments only | [1.3.1 Info and Relationships](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#info-and-relationships) | The span is empty. A screen reader reads nothing for the shortcut | | Positional and OS arguments | [1.3.1 Info and Relationships](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#info-and-relationships) | The span has the positional argument, not the shortcut shown for the user's OS. On a Mac, the page shows ⇧⌘P and the span has "Shift-Ctrl-P" | | Positional argument | [1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#meaningful-sequence) | VoiceOver (VO+Right, Safari) reads the span after the end of the sentence, not where the shortcut is | We found this on quarto.org ([Markdown Basics, Keyboard Shortcuts](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/markdown-basics.html#keyboard-shortcuts)). ### Cause In [`kbd.lua`](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/8680bd68d9083c8f2a575d68168d0e739a004061/src/resources/extensions/quarto/kbd/kbd.lua#L55-L72), the span text is the positional argument, or `""` if there is none. (Lines 57 to 60 set it from the first keyword argument, but line 62 then sets it to `""`.) [`kbd.js`](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/8680bd68d9083c8f2a575d68168d0e739a004061/src/resources/extensions/quarto/kbd/resources/kbd.js#L51-L53) sets the visible text from `data-`, but it does not change the span. The reading order comes from Bootstrap's `.visually-hidden`, which sets `position: absolute !important`. We tested the same markup with a class that does not use absolute positioning. VoiceOver then read the shortcut in place: ```css .kbd-sr { display: inline-block; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip-path: inset(50%); white-space: nowrap; } ``` ### Proposed fix 1. `kbd.js`: when it sets the text from `data-`, also set the text of the span that follows the ``. 2. `kbd.lua`: if there is no positional argument, put `title_str` (all the OS shortcuts) in the span. Then the text is correct when JavaScript does not run. Remove the dead loop at lines 57 to 60. 3. `kbd.lua` and `kbd.css`: give the span a kbd-specific class with the CSS above. Do not change the global `.visually-hidden`. Bootstrap uses it everywhere, and its `!important` rules block a simple override. We also tried the hidden text inside the `` (`⇧⌃PShift-Ctrl-P`). VoiceOver read it in place, but it read the shortcut two times. Related, but not the same: #12919, #13489, #10431, #9542. ## Steps to reproduce ````qmd --- title: kbd repro format: html --- To print, press {{< kbd Shift-Ctrl-P >}}. Then close the dialog. To open a project, press {{< kbd mac=Shift-Command-O win=Shift-Control-O linux=Shift-Ctrl-L >}}. Mixed: {{< kbd Shift-Ctrl-P mac=Shift-Command-P >}}. ```` 1. Render the document. 2. Open it in Safari on macOS. 3. Read each paragraph with VoiceOver (VO+Right). ## Actual behavior DOM after `kbd.js` runs (macOS): ```html ⇧⌃PShift-Ctrl-P ⇧⌘O ⇧⌘PShift-Ctrl-P ``` VoiceOver: - First paragraph: reads "Shift-Ctrl-P" after the end of the sentence. - Second paragraph: reads nothing for the shortcut. - Third paragraph: not tested with VoiceOver. The DOM above shows ⇧⌘P on the page and "Shift-Ctrl-P" in the span. ## Expected behavior A screen reader reads the shortcut that the page shows, at the place where the page shows it. ## Your environment - IDE: none (`quarto render` in the terminal) - Browser: Safari 27.0, with VoiceOver - OS: macOS 27.0 (build 26A428) AI helped investigate. The investigation was grounded in a local clone of quarto-cli. ## Quarto check output ``` Quarto 1.11.6 [✓] Checking environment information... Quarto cache location: /Users/charlottewickham/Library/Caches/quarto Project: none found (single-file mode) [✓] Checking versions of quarto binary dependencies... Pandoc version 3.10.0: OK Dart Sass version 1.101.0: OK Deno version 2.7.14: OK Typst version 0.15.1: OK [✓] Checking versions of quarto dependencies......OK [✓] Checking Quarto installation......OK Version: 1.11.6 Path: /Applications/quarto/bin [✓] Checking tools....................OK TinyTeX: v2026.04 Chrome Headless Shell: 150.0.7871.115 VeraPDF: 1.28.2 [✓] Checking LaTeX....................OK Using: TinyTex Path: /Users/charlottewickham/Library/TinyTeX/bin/universal-darwin Version: 2026 [✓] Checking Chrome Headless....................OK Using: Chrome Headless Shell installed by Quarto Path: /Users/charlottewickham/Library/Application Support/quarto/chrome-headless-shell/chrome-headless-shell-mac-arm64/chrome-headless-shell Version: 150.0.7871.115 [✓] Checking basic markdown render....OK [✓] Checking R installation...........OK Version: 4.6.0 Path: /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.6/Resources LibPaths: - /Users/charlottewickham/Library/R/arm64/4.6/library - /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.6/Resources/library knitr: 1.51 rmarkdown: 2.31 [✓] Checking Knitr engine render......OK [✓] Checking Python 3 installation....OK Version: 3.12.2 Path: /Users/charlottewickham/.pyenv/versions/3.12.2/bin/python3 Jupyter: 5.9.1 Kernels: python3 [✓] Checking Jupyter engine render....OK [✓] Checking Julia installation... ```

title: a11y: footnote back-links have no name except the `↩︎` character
description: ## I have: - [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues - [x] installed the latest version of [Quarto CLI](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/latest) - [x] formatted my issue following the [Bug Reports guide](https://quarto.org/bug-reports.html) ## Bug description Each footnote back-link has the text `↩︎` and no other name. The text is U+21A9 followed by U+FE0E (added by Pandoc for jgm/pandoc#5469, so that iOS does not show an emoji). Move to the back-link at the end of the footnote with VoiceOver. ## Actual behavior ```html ↩︎ ``` VoiceOver reads: > link, leftwards arrow with hook, variation selector 15 ## Expected behavior The link has a name that gives its purpose. title: Website search field is announced as "Submit", or has no name in the overlay
description:
### I have:

- [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues
- [x] installed the latest version of [Quarto CLI](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/latest)
- [x] formatted my issue following the [Bug Reports guide](https://quarto.org/bug-reports.html)

### Bug description

Screen readers announce the website search field as "Submit" with `type: textbox`, and with no name at all with `type: overlay`.

The input gets its name from `aria-labelledby`, which autocomplete points at its own label.
With a text box, that label carries `aria-label="Submit"`, from `search-submit-button-title`.
With the overlay, the input that opens has no name.
Quarto already ships a localised `search-label` ("Search", "Recherche" in French), but it only reaches the `title` of `#quarto-search` and the collapsed-navbar search button, not the input.

An `aria-label` set on the input does not help, because `aria-labelledby` takes precedence.

axe reports no violation, since a name exists, so the accessibility check does not catch it.

This follows #678, which made the referenced label exist: the name that label gives in a text box is "Submit", and the overlay input still has none.

### Steps to reproduce

`_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
project:
  type: website
website:
  title: "Search name"
  navbar:
    left:
      - href: index.qmd
        text: Home
  search:
    location: navbar
    type: textbox
```

`index.qmd`:

```markdown
---
title: "Home"
---

Text.
```

Render the website, serve `_site` over HTTP, and inspect the accessible name of the search input (`.aa-Input`) in the browser's accessibility panel.
Then switch to `type: overlay`, open the search, and inspect the input again.

### Actual behavior

- `type: textbox`: the input is a `searchbox` named "Submit"; `aria-labelledby` points at `<label class="aa-Label" aria-label="Submit">`.
- `type: overlay`: once opened, the input is a `searchbox` with no name.

### Expected behavior

The input is named with the localised `search-label`, "Search" in English, in both layouts.

- OS: macOS 27.0.

title: Dark mode does not set `data-bs-theme`, so Bootstrap colour-mode styles never apply
description:
### I have: - [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues - [x] installed the latest version of [Quarto CLI](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/latest) - [x] formatted my issue following the [Bug Reports guide](https://quarto.org/bug-reports.html) ### Bug description In dark mode, Quarto marks the page with `body.quarto-dark` and swaps the stylesheet bundle, but it never sets `data-bs-theme="dark"`. Bootstrap 5.3 keys its colour-mode rules on that attribute, so Bootstrap components keep their light-mode look on a dark page. The clearest case is `.btn-close`. By default its icon is a black SVG, and Bootstrap only lightens it under `[data-bs-theme="dark"]`. On a dark surface such as a modal, an offcanvas or a toast, the close button is close to invisible. This is also an accessibility problem in Quarto's own output. In a dashboard with light and dark themes and `axe: output: document`, the accessibility report panel stays white in dark mode, while its close button takes the dark theme's white icon. The close button cannot be seen. Setting `data-bs-theme="dark"` by hand makes it show again. ![A dark dashboard with the white Accessibility Report panel open on the right. No close button is visible in the panel header.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6015c732-b407-437a-ad96-08d7eb507897) The navbar already sets `data-bs-theme="dark"` on its own element in `nav-before-body.ejs`, but nothing sets it for the page. ### Steps to reproduce `dark.scss`: ```scss /*-- scss:defaults --*/ $body-bg: #1e1e2e; $body-color: #f0f0f0; ``` `index.qmd`: ````qmd --- title: "Dark mode and Bootstrap colour modes" format: html: theme: light: cosmo dark: [cosmo, dark.scss] --- ```{=html}
Modal header
A dismissible alert.
``` ```` Render, open the page, and switch to dark mode with the toggle. ### Actual behavior After the switch: - `body` has the class `quarto-dark`. - `document.documentElement.getAttribute("data-bs-theme")` is `null`. - `.btn-close` keeps the black icon (`fill='%23000'`) with no `filter`, so it is barely visible on the dark page. - `.alert-warning` keeps its light tint, `rgb(255, 227, 209)`. ### Expected behavior Dark mode sets `data-bs-theme="dark"` on ``, and light mode sets it back to `light`, so Bootstrap's colour-mode rules apply. The close button then turns light on dark surfaces. Setting the attribute by hand in the browser after the switch gives `.btn-close` the filter `invert(1) grayscale(1) brightness(2)`, which comes from the `[data-bs-theme=dark] .btn-close` rule already in the compiled dark bundle. title: Code annotation gutter keeps a grey background when code blocks have none (`code-block-bg: false`)
description:
### I have:

- [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues
- [x] installed the latest version of [Quarto CLI](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/latest)
- [x] formatted my issue following the [Bug Reports guide](https://quarto.org/bug-reports.html)

### Bug description

With `code-block-bg: false`, code blocks have no background, but the code annotation gutter still gets one.
A grey strip shows on the right of every annotated block.

The [HTML code blocks documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/html-code.html) lists `code-block-bg` as a boolean or a colour, and the option sets the `$code-block-bg` Sass variable.
In `src/resources/formats/html/bootstrap/_bootstrap-rules.scss`, `div.sourceCode` checks `$code-block-bg` and falls back to `$body-bg` when it is false.
`.code-annotation-gutter` does not check it and always uses `$code-block-bg-color`:

```scss
.code-annotation-gutter {
  background-color: $code-block-bg-color;
}
```

![An annotated Python code block on a white page with no code background. A light grey strip holding the two annotation markers runs down its right edge.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2a555cf0-5d8b-490e-bbd0-88054b72a444)

### Steps to reproduce

````qmd
---
title: "Annotation gutter"
format: html
code-block-bg: false
code-annotations: below
---

```python
import math  # <1>
x = math.pi  # <2>
```

1. Import.
2. Assign.
````

Two other set-ups give the same result:

- `$code-block-bg: false` in a theme file.
- `code-block-border-left: "#31BAE9"` without `code-block-bg`, because Quarto then sets `$code-block-bg` to false itself (`src/format/html/format-html-scss.ts`).

### Actual behavior

The computed background colours are:

- `div.sourceCode`: `rgb(255, 255, 255)`, the page colour.
- `.code-annotation-gutter`: `rgba(233, 236, 239, 0.65)`.

### Expected behavior

The gutter follows `code-block-bg`, so it has no background of its own when code blocks have none.

title: [FR] Rethink the way to output PDF from any format.
description:
Pandoc does have a simple way to print PDF (https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#creating-a-pdf) 
> To produce a PDF, specify an output file with a .pdf extension:

[--pdf-engine](https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#option--pdf-engine) controls the behavior. Default is to look at the output format, a specific method will be used. 
 * [-t latex](https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#option--to) or none: pdflatex (other options: xelatex, lualatex, tectonic, latexmk)
* [-t context](https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#option--to): context
* [-t html](https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#option--to): wkhtmltopdf (other options: prince, weasyprint, pagedjs-cli; see [print-css.rocks](https://print-css.rocks/) for a good introduction to PDF generation from HTML/CSS)
* [-t ms](https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#option--to): pdfroff
* [-t typst](https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#option--to): typst

Quarto does not really work that way - this currently limit the way to create a PDF, and this is not really consistent across format. 

In Quarto we support `format: pdf` which assumes LaTeX or ConTeXt enine. And `format: typst` which will produce PDF file by default. 

There is special `output-ext` that can modify PDF render. `output-ext: tex` when  `format: pdf` renders a `.tex` file. And `output-ext: typ` when `format: typst` render a `.typ` file. But this variable `output-ext` is fragile (try setting `output-ext` to anything it will not error)

When typst was introduced, `format: typst` has been created but default to render a PDF file. `output-ext` can be use to get the `.typ`. 

HTML printing to PDF is not really supported in Quarto (https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/222). 

Using `format: latex` does not exactly work the same as `format: typst` as it won't produce PDF. 

We should probably rethink all this, and offer more mechanism to create PDF according to method available like Pandoc allows

* Easy and robust way to opt-out PDF for a format that default to it
* Allow printing to PDF from HTML using an external pdf-engine that supports that. 
* Consistent way to produce PDF from Quarto render; or another quarto command (e.g `quarto print`) 

## Related Issues / Discussions

- [ ] https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/222
- [ ] https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/6084
- [ ] https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/discussions/7018
- [ ] https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/4677
- [ ] Removing Pandoc's extension to `--to latex` when using `format: pdf` (https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/6613#issuecomment-1693397040, https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/7966)
- [ ] https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/discussions/9483
- [ ] https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/13314

title: Listing contents: a YAML file next to a folder is silently dropped unless rendering from the listing's directory
description:
With a website project like

```yaml
# _quarto.yml
project:
  type: website
```

and a listing page in a subdirectory, using the pattern from the [YAML Listing Content](https://quarto.org/docs/websites/website-listings.html#yaml-listing-content) docs, a folder plus a YAML file

```markdown
<!-- blog/index.qmd -->
---
title: Blog
listing:
  contents:
    - posts
    - items.yml
---
```

```yaml
# blog/items.yml
- title: "Item from YAML"
  path: https://example.com/item
```

with `blog/posts/post.qmd` titled "Post from folder", the listing depends on where `quarto render` runs.

- From the project root, the listing has "Post from folder" but not "Item from YAML", with no warning.
- From `blog/`, both are listed.

I can reproduce with 1.10.19 and current main.

The docs say the targets of `contents` are identified [relative to the listing page, not the project root](https://quarto.org/docs/websites/website-listings.html#listing-contents). A lone `contents: items.yml` is resolved that way and works from any directory. It is only when the folder and the file are mixed that the file is resolved against the working directory.

A few related symptoms from the same code:

- If a file with the same name exists in the working directory, it is listed instead of the one next to the listing page.
- `contents: [posts, /items.yml]` is dropped whatever the working directory, since the anchored path is read as the filesystem root.
- `contents: [posts, posts/post.qmd]` lists the post twice when rendering from `blog/`.

The loop that adds named files that are not project inputs checks existence and builds the path from `Deno.cwd()`:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/53fda8160f1bc05cebbed182977a0aebae5de3aa/src/project/types/website/listing/website-listing-read.ts#L763-L770

It was added in 4ad0f0004 and has worked this way since. It goes unnoticed when the listing page is at the project root and the render runs from there, since both bases are the same.

Same dependence on the working directory as #15039 for image paths.

title: Upgrade Mermaid to 11.17.2 (fixes six advisories in 11.12.x)
description:
quarto-cli vendors Mermaid 11.12.0 in `src/resources/formats/html/mermaid/`. Every rendered HTML page that uses Mermaid ships it. Six advisories affect all 11.12.x releases, and they're fixed in 11.14.1 or 11.16.1:

- GHSA-c4c3-pg64-4m4v
- GHSA-6x64-9x62-f2gx
- GHSA-87f9-hvmw-gh4p
- GHSA-xcj9-5m2h-648r
- GHSA-ghcm-xqfw-q4vr
- GHSA-6m6c-36f7-fhxh

They cover config prototype pollution, CSS/`classDef` and HTML injection, and an infinite loop in Gantt charts. 11.17.2 has none of them.

**Proposal:** bump to 11.17.2. That would match the VS Code extension, which moved its notebook renderer and its diagram preview to 11.17.2 in quarto-dev/quarto#1189. Both now run ahead of the CLI's Mermaid version.

As in `dev-docs/upgrade-dependencies.md`, get `dist/mermaid.js` and `dist/mermaid.min.js` from `https://unpkg.com/mermaid@11.17.2/` and copy them into `src/resources/formats/html/mermaid/`.

**Things to know about 11.13 to 11.17:**
- These releases mostly add syntax (new diagram types and shapes, extra directives), so existing diagrams should keep working.
- One visible change: in 11.17, `classDiagram` and C4 diagrams moved to Mermaid's unified (v2) renderer, so they'll look somewhat different.
- 11.17 builds no longer embed `name:"mermaid",version:"…"` in the bundle. Anything that sniffs the version from the file needs another pattern; the extension's test now matches the `renderer.draw(…, "X.Y.Z"` literal.
- `mermaid.min.js` grows from 2.75 MB to 3.57 MB.

title: a11y: `quarto create project blog` scaffold has images with no alt text and icon-only navbar links with no name
description: The blog scaffold from `quarto create project blog` fails WCAG 2.x Level A right after it is created. It has three images with no alternative text and two icon-only navbar links with no accessible name. The templates already support all the fixes. The scaffold content does not use them. New authors copy the scaffold as their model, so it should show the accessible pattern. ## Reproduce (Quarto 1.11.5) ```sh quarto create project blog blog quarto render blog quarto call axe blog/_site ``` axe-core 4.10.3, 4 pages, 1440x900 and 320x568: | Rule (WCAG) | Element | Source in scaffold | |---|---|---| | `image-alt` (1.1.1) | `` on `about.html` | `about.qmd`: `image: profile.jpg`, no `image-alt` | | `image-alt` (1.1.1) | listing thumbnail, Post With Code | `posts/post-with-code/index.qmd`: `image: "image.jpg"`, no `image-alt` | | `image-alt` (1.1.1) | `` in Welcome post body, and its listing card | `posts/welcome/index.qmd`: `![](thumbnail.jpg)` | | `link-name` (2.4.4, 4.1.2) | both listing thumbnail links (an image link with no alt has no name) | follows from the two rows above | | `link-name` (2.4.4, 4.1.2), `role-img-alt` (1.1.1) | navbar GitHub and Bluesky links, every page | `_quarto.yml`: `- icon: github` / `- icon: bluesky` with no `text` or `aria-label` | ## Proposed scaffold changes All in `src/project/types/website/website.ts` (blog scaffold content) and `src/resources/projects/website/templates/blog/_quarto-blog.ejs.yml`. `_quarto.yml`: ```yaml navbar: right: - about.qmd - icon: github href: https://github.com/ aria-label: GitHub - icon: bluesky href: https://bsky.app/ aria-label: Bluesky ``` `about.qmd`: ```yaml image: profile.jpg image-alt: "A stick figure drawn in light against a dusk sky" ``` `posts/post-with-code/index.qmd`: ```yaml image: "image.jpg" image-alt: "City lights across Earth at night, seen from orbit" ``` `posts/welcome/index.qmd`: ```markdown ![](thumbnail.jpg){fig-alt="A laptop, a cup of coffee, a notepad and a phone on a wooden desk"} ``` ## Result The same scan with all four changes: every `image-alt`, `link-name` and `role-img-alt` finding is cleared (10 findings → 0). The findings that remain have their own issues: listing category contrast (#14381) and the best-practice landmark and heading-order findings (#14375/#14377/#14384/#14605). ## Other `quarto create` scaffolds We checked the 1.11.5 project templates (`default`, `website`, `book`, `manuscript`, `confluence`). Only the blog sets `image:` or uses icon-only navbar items. The book scaffold copies `cover.png` into the project, but its `_quarto.yml` does not set `cover-image`, so nothing renders it. When an author adds `cover-image`, they need `cover-image-alt` too. This is outside the scope of this issue. ## Related - #14828: `navbar: tools:` / `sidebar: tools:` with only `icon:` get `aria-label=""`. That path is a different template (`navtools.ejs`). The blog's `navbar: right:` items go through `navitem.ejs`/`navicon.ejs`. There, `aria-label:` already works, but there is no fallback when it is not set. The icon-name fallback proposed in #14828 should also cover this path. This issue only changes the scaffold, so the blog is correct with or without that fallback. - #7979 (closed 2023-12): added `image-alt` support to about pages. The scaffold was not updated to use it. - #7028: listing image alt.

title: PDF render with `lang: de-CH` fails when `hyphen-german` is not installed
description:
When rendering to PDF with `lang: de-CH` on a TinyTeX that has no German hyphenation patterns, Quarto installs `babel-german` but the compilation still fails, and `hyphen-german` is never installed.

First reported at rstudio/tinytex#515.

## Reproduction

TinyTeX without `hyphen-german` and `babel-german` (fresh install, or after `tinytex::tlmgr_remove()`):

````qmd
---
title: "Untitled"
lang: de-CH
format: pdf
---

Hallo Welt.
````

## Actual behavior

`babel-german` is installed automatically, then the render aborts:

```
! Package babel Error: You haven't defined the language 'ngerman' yet.
(babel)                Perhaps you misspelled it or your installation
(babel)                is not complete.
```

`babel-german` checks `\iflanguage{ngerman}` at `\begin{document}`, and without the hyphenation patterns of `hyphen-german` babel treats the language as undefined. Missing hyphenation patterns are only handled by Quarto when babel reports them as a warning on a successful compile, so this fatal error finds nothing to install.

I can reproduce on current main (a57cc7645). After the failed render, `tinytex::tlmgr_install("hyphen-german")` makes the same document render.

## Expected behavior

Quarto installs `hyphen-german` and the render succeeds, as it does for other languages.

We could detect this babel error on the failure path and install the matching `hyphen-<lang>` package.

Related: #12732, #10291

title: revealjs: off-screen slides stay in the keyboard tab order (Tab from slide N lands on slide N-2)
description:
### I have:

- [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues
- [ ] installed the latest version of [Quarto CLI](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/latest)
- [x] formatted my issue following the [Bug Reports guide](https://quarto.org/bug-reports.html)

### Bug description

In a Quarto `revealjs` deck, <kbd>Tab</kbd> does not reach the current slide's content first. Focusable elements on `.past`/`.future` slides inside `viewDistance` stay in the tab order, so a keyboard user tabs into slides that are not on screen with nothing to tell them they have left the slide they were reading. This is a WCAG 2.4.3 (Focus Order) failure in output Quarto produces.

The intent is already in the markup — reveal.js sets both `hidden` and `aria-hidden="true"` on non-present slides — but neither takes effect:

- reveal also writes an inline `display: block` on every slide inside `viewDistance`. An inline declaration outranks the UA stylesheet's `[hidden] { display: none }`, so `hidden` has no effect and the subtree stays tabbable.
- `aria-hidden="true"` hides the subtree from assistive technology but has no bearing on the tab order.

The result is slides that are announced as hidden and are reachable by <kbd>Tab</kbd> at the same time.

DOM on slide 5 of a ten-slide deck (`viewDistance: 3`, the Quarto default):

```
slide-3  .past     hidden  aria-hidden="true"  style="display: block"
slide-4  .past     hidden  aria-hidden="true"  style="display: block"
slide-5  .present  -       -                   style="display: block"
slide-6  .future   hidden  aria-hidden="true"  style="display: block"
slide-7  .future   hidden  aria-hidden="true"  style="display: block"
slide-8  .future   hidden  aria-hidden="true"  style="display: none"
```

Slides outside `viewDistance` get `display: none` and leave the tab order correctly. The ones inside it do not.

### Why I think this belongs in Quarto rather than upstream alone

Upstream is [hakimel/reveal.js#1587](https://github.com/hakimel/reveal.js/issues/1587), open since May 2016. The answer given in that thread is "use the a11y plugin", meaning [marcysutton/reveal-a11y](https://github.com/marcysutton/reveal-a11y) — last commit June 2020, written against the pre-4.x plugin API, and not bundled with Quarto. Quarto's bundled revealjs plugins are `chalkboard`, `line-highlight`, `menu`, `multiplex`, `pdfexport`, `support`, `tone`; none of them handles this, and `grep -r inert` over the bundled revealjs resources returns nothing relevant.

The other route users are pointed at is the third-party [mcanouil/quarto-revealjs-a11y](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-revealjs-a11y) extension, whose `slide-landmarks` feature targets exactly this. It is opt-in, and its current release has two defects that make it unreliable for the content that suffers most from the bug — see [mcanouil/quarto-revealjs-a11y#25](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-revealjs-a11y/issues/25): elements focusable only through `tabindex` are demoted and never restored, and `iframe` is never demoted at all.

So both routes are currently unavailable or unreliable, while the defect ships in Quarto's own output. A patch in Quarto seems right until upstream lands a fix, at which point it can be dropped.

### On the `tabindex` approaches, and why `inert` is the one that holds up

| approach | outcome |
|---|---|
| `hidden` on the section | already applied by reveal; defeated by the inline `display: block` written on the same element |
| `aria-hidden="true"` | already applied; hides from AT, no effect on tab order |
| per-element `tabindex="-1"` with save/restore | needs an accurate list of what is focusable, plus per-element state to restore the author's original value. The list is easy to get wrong: `iframe`, `audio[controls]`, `video[controls]`, `summary` and `[contenteditable]` are tabbable with no `tabindex` attribute at all, and `tabindex="0"` on an author's own widget has to be preserved, not dropped. The restore pass then has to find elements it has itself demoted — which is exactly where the third-party extension breaks. |
| `inert` on the section | one attribute per slide, no per-element state, no focusable-element list to keep in sync. Removes the subtree from the tab order *and* the accessibility tree. Not display-based, so the inline `display: block` does not defeat it. [Baseline](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/inert) across Chrome, Safari and Firefox since April 2023. |

### Proposed patch

```js
function updateInertSlides() {
  const current = Reveal.getCurrentSlide();
  document.querySelectorAll(".reveal .slides section").forEach((s) => {
    s.toggleAttribute("inert", !(s === current || s.contains(current)));
  });
}
function clearInertSlides() {
  document
    .querySelectorAll(".reveal .slides section[inert]")
    .forEach((s) => s.removeAttribute("inert"));
}
Reveal.on("ready", updateInertSlides);
Reveal.on("slidechanged", updateInertSlides);
Reveal.on("overviewshown", clearInertSlides);
Reveal.on("overviewhidden", updateInertSlides);
```

`s.contains(current)` keeps a vertical stack's ancestor reachable while its non-present siblings go inert. Overview mode needs the escape hatch because every slide is legitimately on screen there; the print/PDF and scroll views need the same treatment, which I would cover in the PR.

I would be glad to open the PR — say where you would want it to live (the bundled `support` plugin, a new bundled plugin, or the reveal init in `revealjs.ts`) and whether it should be unconditional or sit behind a format option, and I will send it that way.

### Steps to reproduce

A deck with nothing but links reproduces it — no code cells or extensions involved:

````qmd
---
title: "Tab order probe"
format: revealjs
---

## Slide 1 {#slide-1}

[link on slide 1](https://example.com/1)

## Slide 2 {#slide-2}

[link on slide 2](https://example.com/2)

<!-- ... repeat through slide 10 ... -->
````

```bash
quarto render deck.qmd
```

Open `deck.html#/slide-5`, click nothing, and press <kbd>Tab</kbd>.

### Actual behavior

On slide 5, the first four <kbd>Tab</kbd> presses go:

```
Tab 1 -> "link on slide 3"   section#slide-3  .past      (off screen)
Tab 2 -> "link on slide 4"   section#slide-4  .past      (off screen)
Tab 3 -> "link on slide 5"   section#slide-5  .present   (the slide on screen)
Tab 4 -> "link on slide 6"   section#slide-6  .future    (off screen)
```

The reader has to tab past two invisible slides to reach the one they are on, and tabbing once more takes them off it again. Nothing is announced at either boundary, because those sections carry `aria-hidden="true"`.

Measured in Chrome by dispatching real key presses and reading `document.activeElement` after each.

The impact scales with embedded interactive content. I maintain [maidr](https://github.com/xability/maidr), which renders charts a blind reader explores from the keyboard; on a ten-slide deck with one chart per slide the reader lands inside a chart belonging to a slide they are not on, and the chart takes over the arrow keys once focused.

### Expected behavior

<kbd>Tab</kbd> from the current slide reaches that slide's own content first, and does not reach content on slides that are not on screen.

With the patch above applied to the same deck:

```
on slide 5:  Tab 1 -> "link on slide 5"  section#slide-5  .present
             Tab 2 -> deck menu button (outside .slides)
             Tab 3 -> leaves the document
Space     -> slide 6
on slide 6:  Tab 1 -> "link on slide 6"  section#slide-6  .present
o         -> overview: inert cleared on all 11 sections
Escape    -> back to slide 6, inert restored to the other 10
```

Verified in Chrome on the deck above. Transitions and slide navigation are unaffected.

### Your environment

- IDE: none (rendered from the command line)
- OS: Windows 11 26200
- Browser: Chrome
- reveal.js: 5.1.0 (`Reveal.VERSION`, as bundled by Quarto)

Reproduced on Quarto **1.8.27** (the `quarto check` below) and on **1.10.18** on Linux. Both bundle reveal.js 5.1.0 and behave identically, which is expected since the behaviour comes from that bundle rather than from Quarto's own code.

title: Notebook preview page missing from `_site` when rendering a website from outside its directory
description:
### I have:

- [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues
- [x] installed the latest version of [Quarto CLI](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/latest)
- [x] formatted my issue following the [Bug Reports guide](https://quarto.org/bug-reports.html)

### Bug description

When a website project embeds a notebook and is rendered from another directory (`quarto render my-site` or `quarto render my-site/index.qmd`), the notebook preview page is not in `_site`. The embed in `index.html` still links to it, so the link is a 404. The notebook download source is missing too. Rendering with the project directory as working directory works.

This is not a regression, I see the same with 1.4.557, 1.10.19 and current `main`.

The notebook preview step forwards its outputs as supporting files using paths relative to the project directory

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/83097c10af6bc5dd50a79b66739f1e34843ee3fb/src/format/html/format-html-notebook-preview.ts#L226-L255

but HTML postprocessor supporting files are expected to be absolute paths

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/83097c10af6bc5dd50a79b66739f1e34843ee3fb/src/command/render/types.ts#L99-L100

and the render step filters them with `existsSync` before making them relative to the project directory

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/83097c10af6bc5dd50a79b66739f1e34843ee3fb/src/command/render/render.ts#L443-L446

`existsSync` on a relative path resolves against the working directory. So these entries are kept only when the working directory is the project directory. Otherwise they are dropped, never moved to `_site`, and the notebook cleanup deletes the preview from the source directory.

This also affects our Playwright tests, which render every fixture from `tests/`, so a fixture relying on a notebook preview page in a website gets a 404 there (found while adding a test for #14972).

Related: #10756 (also a missing notebook preview in a website, but triggered by `freeze`)

### Steps to reproduce

`my-site/_quarto.yml`

```yaml
project:
  type: website
```

`my-site/index.qmd`

````qmd
---
title: Home
---

{{< embed computations.qmd#answer >}}
````

`my-site/computations.qmd`

````qmd
---
title: Computations
jupyter: python3
---

```{python}
#| label: answer
print(42)
```
````

From the parent directory of `my-site`:

```bash
quarto render my-site
```

Then compare with rendering from inside the project:

```bash
cd my-site
quarto render
```

The same happens with an embedded `.ipynb` (`*-preview.html`, `*.out.ipynb` and the notebook figures in `*_files/` missing, the latter left behind in the source directory).

### Actual behavior

From the parent directory, `my-site/_site` contains only `computations.html`, `index.html`, `search.json` and `site_libs`, while `index.html` links to `computations.embed-preview.html`.

### Expected behavior

`_site` contains `computations.embed-preview.html` and `computations.qmd` whatever the working directory, as it does when rendering from inside `my-site`.

### Your environment

- OS: Windows 11
- Not specific to the IDE, reproduced from the command line

### Quarto check output

Reproduced with Quarto 1.4.557, 1.10.19 and 1.11 dev (`main` at 83097c10a). Not dependent on the environment, the logic is in the render code linked above.

title: Keyboard tabbing order of tabset tabs and focusable controls within tabset content
description:
I'm seeing some inconsistency with the keyboard tabbing order when I use tabsets.

In [this example](https://github.com/360-info/report-global-education/blob/main/embed-bycountry.qmd), in which I've styled the tabs to appear at the bottom of the page ([deployed version available here](https://360info-studentflows.pages.dev/embed-bycountry)), the tabs have `tabindex="0"` and so are tabbable - but tabbing to put focus on them activates them, so it's impossible to then tab onto focusable elements within the tabset content (eg. checkboxes or dropdowns) unless you click on one of them first.

In the following example, the tabs aren't receiving any `tabindex` attribute at all and so aren't tabbable:

````
---
title: "Test tabs"
author: "jimjamslam"
---

Let's try some tabs!

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Tab A

This is just some explanatory text. No biggie...

## Tab B

Let's add some focusable controls here!

```{ojs}
viewof catSelect = Inputs.select(
  ["Apple", "Banana", "Orange", "Kiwi"],
  { label: "Choose a fruit"});

viewof numSelect = Inputs.range([1, 20], { label: "And a number" });
```

## Tab C

Some more text here! Could be lots of stuff.

```{ojs}
viewof check = Inputs.checkbox(
  ["Don't forget to check this!"],
  { label: "Options" })
```
## Tab D

Nah, this is all boring.

:::
````

Ideally, I expect that tabset tabs would be tabbable, but that tabbing onto a different tab would focus it without activating it so that I could continue on to any controls visible (unless I explicitly activated it as I might a hyperlink).

I'm not quite sure why the tabs in my first example have `tabindex` and the ones in my second don't, unless there's been a change in behaviour that I missed (although I believe I rendered them both with them same versions of everything). (Maybe the styling I used on the tabs in the first, adding `display: flex` and `flex-direction: column-reverse` to `.panel-tabset` to put the tabs below the content, did something weird?)

I think I've said "tab" enough for the rest of the year now 😂

title: Update bundled reveal.js to 6.x
description:
We still bundle reveal.js 5.1.0 (we never took 5.2.x).

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/83097c10af6bc5dd50a79b66739f1e34843ee3fb/configuration#L43

reveal.js 6.0 is a major release with breaking path changes (plugins move from `plugin/<name>` to `dist/plugin/`, `.esm.js` becomes `.mjs`), so this affects how we vendor it and how we resolve plugins. Upgrade guide: https://revealjs.com/upgrading/

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/83097c10af6bc5dd50a79b66739f1e34843ee3fb/package/src/common/update-html-dependencies.ts#L293-L310

Bundled third-party plugins (chalkboard, menu, pdfexport, multiplex) need to be checked against the 6.x API too.

## What we would get

- Off-screen slides marked `inert` so Tab stays on the current slide (6.0.2, hakimel/reveal.js#1587). We are planning a stopgap in our `support` plugin for #14795, which mirrors upstream's condition and can be removed with this update.
- MathJax 4 support (see #14712).

## Note for the axe check

reveal.js 6.0.2 sets `inert` on every non-present slide. axe-core treats an inert subtree as hidden, and our axe check only lifts `hidden` and `aria-hidden` before scanning all slides:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/83097c10af6bc5dd50a79b66739f1e34843ee3fb/src/resources/formats/html/axe/axe-check.js#L474-L499

So with 6.x the axe check also needs to remove `inert` during the scan and set it back after, otherwise violations on other slides silently stop being reported. The fix for #14795 should already include this change. In that case this update only removes the `support` plugin stopgap and keeps the axe part.

## Related

- #14795
- #14712

title: Embeded chunks do not respect the "execute-dir: project" setting
description:
### Bug description

I have a quarto project, in which I have set the "execute-dir: project" in the yml file. This is because I have data files in one folder in the project dir, and quarto notebooks in a docs folder. When an individual notebook loads data files it works. However, if I embed a chunk from such a notebook into another, suddenly I get an error that the file cannot be found. Seems like rendering of notebooks to embed them does not respect the execture-dir: project setting.

### Steps to reproduce

``` r
# create a quarto website project
tmp <- tempfile()
dir.create(tmp)
setwd(tmp)
system("quarto create project website .")

# create a file in a folder
dir.create("inner")
file.copy("about.qmd", "inner/file.qmd")

# write a code chunk in the inner file to open a file in base directory
saveRDS(rnorm(10), "data.rds")
```

title: revealjs tabset tabs get positive tabindex values
description:
## I have:

- [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues
- [x] installed the latest version of [Quarto CLI](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/latest)
- [x] formatted my issue following the [Bug Reports guide](https://quarto.org/bug-reports.html)

## Bug description

In a `revealjs` deck, tabset tabs get `tabindex="1"`, `"2"`, and so on. Positive values put the tabs before all other content in the Tab order. As a result, on the 2 slides before a tabset, the first <kbd>Tab</kbd> moves focus to a tab on a slide that is not visible. This breaks [WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.3 Focus Order](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#focus-order).

- **Cause:** when `body.reveal-viewport` is present, Quarto's copy of `tabby.js` gives each tab, and each focusable element in each tab panel, the next positive tabindex ([tabby.js#L314-L336](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/abc6a78ed68f9e8bc9d54e27851093bd687a1cb7/src/resources/formats/html/tabby/js/tabby.js#L314-L336), from a174f59).
- **Impact:** keyboard users lose focus to a tab on a slide that is not visible. There is no visible focus and no slide change.
- **Fix:** use `tabindex="0"` in revealjs too (the non-reveal branch), or a roving tabindex (`0` on the selected tab, `-1` on the others).

Related: #14795 (off-screen slides stay in the tab order). Positive tabindex makes that problem worse, because the tabs come before the content of the current slide.

AI note: I used an AI assistant to investigate. Its findings are grounded in a local clone of quarto-cli.

## Steps to reproduce

````qmd
---
format: revealjs
---

## Slide 1

Plain slide.

## Slide 2

Plain slide.

## Slide 3

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Tab A

Content A

### Tab B

Content B

:::
````

1. Render the file and open it in Chrome.
2. On slide 1, press <kbd>Tab</kbd>.
3. Go to slide 2, then press <kbd>Tab</kbd>.

## Actual behavior

- On slide 1, focus moves to "Tab A" (`tabindex="1"`) on slide 3, which is not visible.
- On slide 2, focus moves to "Tab B" (`tabindex="2"`) on slide 3, which is not visible.
- The slide does not change, and nothing on screen shows focus.

## Expected behavior

Focus moves in DOM order to content on the current slide. The tabs have `tabindex="0"` (or `-1` for tabs that are not selected), as they do in HTML output.

## Your environment

- IDE: none (rendered with the CLI, tested in Chrome 154.0.8037.58)
- OS: macOS 26.6.2 (build 25G83)

title: revealjs format extension `logo:` resolves to a broken path in subfolder documents when the project has a `_brand.yml`
description: # I have: - [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues - [x] installed the latest version of Quarto CLI (1.10.18) - [x] formatted my issue following the Bug Reports guide # Bug description A revealjs **format extension** that sets `logo:` (path relative to the extension folder) works in a website project until the project also has a `brand:` file. With a brand file, documents in a **subdirectory** get ``, a path that points outside `_site` and is not copied into the output, so the logo 404s once the site is deployed. Documents in the project root are fine, and without `brand:` the logo is correctly copied to `site_libs/quarto-contrib/...` for both. This looks like the same root cause described in #14075 (project-relative logo paths corrected to document-relative paths after merging with brand), which fixed Typst only and noted "related bugs in dashboard and revealjs which might need a similar fix". Related: #11982 (brand logo paths in subdirectories; closed). The brand file does not need to contain a logo. Its mere presence changes how the extension's `logo:` is resolved. # How this was found I maintain a Quarto course website and was extracting its slide theme into a reusable format extension, [quarto-lmu-revealjs](https://github.com/cynthiahqy/quarto-lmu-revealjs), used by a website template, [quarto-lmu-subject-template](https://github.com/cynthiahqy/quarto-lmu-subject-template). The extension originally set `logo:` in its `_extension.yml`. Slides in the project root showed the logo, but slides in week subfolders (`02-topic/slides.qmd`) had a broken image, because the rendered path was `../../_extensions/lmu/logos/...`, which is outside `_site` and never copied. Testing showed the trigger is a `brand:` entry in `_quarto.yml` (removing it makes the subfolder logo work). The minimal repro below is independent of those repos. Workaround currently used in the template: the extension no longer sets a default `logo:`, and the logo is set in the project instead (`_brand.yml` `logo:` and a project-root-relative `logo:` in `_slides.yml`). See `_brand.yml` and `_slides.yml` in the template repo. **Disclosure:** this report was drafted by an AI assistant (Claude Sonnet 5, via Claude Code) working in my repository. The repro was run and its output observed on Quarto 1.10.18 in that session; I have reviewed the text before posting. # Steps to reproduce ``` . ├── _extensions/repro/ │ ├── _extension.yml │ └── logo.png # any png ├── _brand.yml ├── _quarto.yml ├── root.qmd └── sub/deck.qmd ``` `_extensions/repro/_extension.yml` ```yaml title: Repro author: x version: 1.0.0 contributes: formats: revealjs: logo: logo.png ``` `_quarto.yml` ```yaml project: type: website brand: _brand.yml ``` `_brand.yml` ```yaml color: primary: "#00883A" ``` `root.qmd` and `sub/deck.qmd` (identical apart from title) ```markdown --- title: test format: repro-revealjs --- ## slide ``` ```bash quarto render grep -o '' _site/root.html _site/sub/deck.html find _site -name logo.png ``` # Actual behavior With `brand: _brand.yml`: ``` _site/root.html: _site/sub/deck.html: ``` Only `_site/site_libs/quarto-contrib/quarto-project/repro/logo.png` exists. The `../../_extensions/...` path from `_site/sub/` resolves outside the output directory. # Expected behavior `sub/deck.html` should reference `../site_libs/quarto-contrib/quarto-project/repro/logo.png`, as it does when `brand:` is removed from `_quarto.yml`. # Notes - Removing `brand:` from `_quarto.yml` makes both documents correct. - Setting the logo in the project instead (e.g. `logo:` in `_brand.yml`, or a project-root-relative `logo:` in document metadata) works; only the extension-provided default is affected. - `format-resources` and `logo: {path: ...}` in the extension did not change the result. # Your environment - macOS (Darwin 25.6.0), Quarto CLI 1.10.18 (Homebrew cask) - Also observed on 1.9.36 # Quarto check output ``` Quarto 1.10.18 [✓] Checking environment information... title: Hugo project detection matches a parent folder whose `config/` can't be entered, so `quarto render` can silently write Markdown
description:
### I have:

- [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues
- [x] installed the latest version of Quarto CLI
- [x] formatted my issue following the Bug Reports guide

### Bug description

`quarto render doc.qmd --output doc.html` can exit 0, print `Output created: doc.html`, and write Hugo Markdown into `doc.html` instead of HTML, with no warning. This happens when:
- a parent folder has a `content/` folder and a `config/` folder that Quarto can list but can't enter (read but no execute permission, e.g. mode 644), and
- neither the document's folder nor any parent has a `_quarto.yml`.

Quarto detects that parent folder as a Hugo project. The bundled Hugo extension's detect rule `["config/_default/config.toml", "content"]` matches, although `config.toml` does not exist. With `config/` at mode 644 the render silently produces hugo-md; at mode 000 it fails.

This isn't covered by #14966; I tested on `main` 04e3341. I filed this earlier without the template as #14980, which was closed as a duplicate of #14960.

**Cause.** The detector check `files.every((file) => safeExistsSync(join(dir, file)))` (`src/project/project-context.ts`) calls `safeExistsSync`, which wraps `@std/fs` `existsSync` in a `catch` that returns `false`. But `existsSync` (`@std/fs` 1.0.16) deliberately returns `true` on `PermissionDenied` rather than throwing (its comment: "the item exists, but can't be read"), so that catch never sees permission errors. With `p/config` at mode 000, `existsSync("p/config/_default/config.toml")` returns `true`, although `p/config/_default` doesn't exist either. For a path whose lookup is denied, such as one below a folder that can't be entered, a permission error says nothing about whether the item exists, so "exists" is the wrong answer for project detection. The inaccessible folder isn't Quarto's problem; treating it as proof that `config/_default/config.toml` exists is.

**Why the #14966 message doesn't help.** In the 644 case there's no error at all. In the 000 case it says *"remove the files that mark it as one. Otherwise make the directory readable."* Here the marker it relies on, `config/_default/config.toml`, doesn't exist.

**Where we hit this** (Quarto 1.7.31; 1.10.18 fails the same way): a FUSE mount of S3, where a folder at the top of the mount has `config` and `content` entries we can't access, so looking up `config/_default` gives permission denied rather than not found. Quarto made that folder the project and tried to create its cache, `.quarto/project-cache`, there. The mount refused to create the file, and the render failed with `attempt to write a readonly database`. `main` has the same detection logic (see the steps below). With the `stat` check proposed below, that folder isn't detected either.

**Workaround.** A `_quarto.yml` in the document's folder, or in any folder above it but below `p`, avoids this, but it makes that folder a project.

### Steps to reproduce

Run this as a non-root user (root bypasses permission checks). After each render the block prints the exit code; after renders 1 and 2, `head` shows the start of `doc.html`.
- Render 1 writes HTML (`<!DOCTYPE html>`).
- With `config/` at mode 644 (listable, but not enterable), render 2 exits 0 and prints `Output created: doc.html`, but the file starts with `---`: it is Markdown.
- With `config/` at mode 000, render 3 fails.

The last line restores the folder so it can be deleted.

```bash
cd "$(mktemp -d)"
mkdir -p p/config p/content p/work
printf -- '---\ntitle: t\n---\nhi\n' > p/work/doc.qmd
(cd p/work && quarto render doc.qmd --output doc.html); echo "exit $?"
head -c 15 p/work/doc.html; echo
chmod 644 p/config
(cd p/work && quarto render doc.qmd --output doc.html); echo "exit $?"
head -c 15 p/work/doc.html; echo
chmod 000 p/config
(cd p/work && quarto render doc.qmd --output doc.html); echo "exit $?"
chmod 755 p/config
```

### Actual behavior

On Quarto 1.10.18, and on `main` 04e3341, which includes #14966 (the 1.11.5 pre-release predates it):

- **Render 2:** exits 0, but `doc.html` is 22 bytes of Markdown: the front matter and `hi`.
  - `quarto inspect doc.qmd` reports format `hugo-md` and project dir `p`.
  - `p/.quarto` is created.
  - Without `--output`, the render writes `doc.md`.
- **Render 3:** fails. Run in `p/work`, with stack traces trimmed. On 1.10.18:
```
$ quarto render doc.qmd --output doc.html
ERROR: PermissionDenied: Permission denied (os error 13): readdir '.../p/config'
```
On `main`:
```
$ quarto render doc.qmd --output doc.html
ERROR: Could not read a directory while looking for project input files.
✖ Permission denied (os error 13): readdir '.../p/config'
ℹ Project root: .../p (detected by an extension project type, no _quarto.yml)
ℹ If this directory is not meant to be a Quarto project, remove the files that mark it as one. Otherwise make the directory readable.
```

1.7.31 behaves the same: Markdown at 644, and a `WalkError` at 000.

### Expected behavior

All three renders should write HTML, as the first does: a single-file render, with no project. A detect path whose existence can't be checked shouldn't satisfy a rule. Only detection would change; the input walk would still fail on unreadable folders, as #14966 intends.

One option: count a detect path only if it can be stat'ed.

```ts
files.every((file) => { try { Deno.statSync(join(dir, file)); return true; } catch { return false; } })
```

`existsSync(path, { isReadable: true })` would stop this match too, but it would also drop detection when the config file itself is unreadable; `stat` doesn't.

I tested this on `main` (macOS):
- All three renders above write HTML, and no `p/.quarto` is created.
- All three Hugo rules and docusaurus are still detected, including with an unreadable config file or `package.json`.
- A real Hugo site with `config/` at mode 111 is still detected, and its walk then fails with #14966's error.
- The trade-off: a real Hugo site that relies on `config/_default/config.toml`, and whose `config/` the renderer can't enter, is no longer detected, and renders as a single file. Today it renders hugo-md at mode 644 and fails at 000. That is the same result as if the config file were absent, which is all Quarto can verify.

Failing at detection instead, with #14966's error, would also end the silent Markdown. But every render below such a folder would then fail, and unless they can fix the permissions, the user would need a `_quarto.yml` to opt out of a project they never had.

### Your environment

- IDE: none (terminal)
- OS: macOS 26.7 (Quarto 1.10.18 and `main`); also reproduced on Ubuntu 22.04.5 x86_64 (Quarto 1.10.18)

title: Safari scrollbar workaround in color scheme init resets scroll position and breaks fragment navigation
description:
### I have:

- [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues
- [x] installed the latest version of [Quarto CLI](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/latest)
- [x] formatted my issue following the [Bug Reports guide](https://quarto.org/bug-reports.html)

### Bug description

On page load, Safari sometimes ignores the URL fragment and leaves the page at the top.
The cause is the Safari-only scrollbar workaround (#1455) in `quarto-html-before-body.ejs`:

```js
if (navigator.userAgent.indexOf('Safari') > 0 && navigator.userAgent.indexOf('Chrome') == -1) {
  manageTransitions("body", false);
  window.scrollTo(0, 1);
  setTimeout(() => {
    window.scrollTo(0, 0);
    manageTransitions("body", true);
  }, 40);
}
```

This code is in `toggleColorMode()`, which the inline script at the start of `<body>` calls on every load (`toggleColorMode(false)` or `toggleColorMode(true)`).
The 40 ms timer races with the browser's scroll to the fragment target.
On a large page, parsing blocks the main thread for longer than 40 ms.
Then the timer fires after the fragment scroll, and `window.scrollTo(0, 0)` returns the page to the top.

I wrapped `window.scrollTo` early in the load and recorded a failing run (times are `performance.now()` in ms):

```
594  load y=121264                          <- Safari scrolled to the fragment target
640  window.scrollTo [0,0] y=121264 :: https://docs.posit.co/connect/admin/appendix/configuration/:201:26
642  scroll event y=0
```

Line 201 of that page is the `window.scrollTo(0, 0)` call above.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Save this document as `index.qmd`:

   ````markdown
   ---
   title: "Safari fragment repro"
   format:
     html:
       theme:
         light: flatly
         dark: darkly
   ---

   {{< lipsum 1000 >}}

   ## Target {#target}

   The page must open here.

   {{< lipsum 50 >}}
   ````

2. Run `quarto render index.qmd`.
3. Serve the folder over HTTP, for example with `python3 -m http.server 8000`.
4. In Safari, open <http://localhost:8000/index.html#target>.
5. Press Command-L, then press Enter to load the URL again.

In my tests, the page stayed at the top on 10 of 10 reloads.
Then I removed only the `window.scrollTo(0, 1)` and `window.scrollTo(0, 0)` calls from the rendered `index.html`.
With that change, the page scrolled to `#target` on 10 of 10 reloads.
The same document with a single theme (`format: html`) does not include the workaround, and it also scrolled to `#target` every time.

The problem also occurs on a production site: <https://docs.posit.co/connect/admin/appendix/configuration/#GitCredential.Password> (Quarto 1.9.32) stayed at the top on 2 to 3 of every 10 reloads.

### Actual behavior

The page sometimes stays at the top, and the fragment target is not visible.

### Expected behavior

The page always scrolls to the fragment target, as in Chrome, Edge, and Firefox.

### Possible fix

Run the workaround only when the user toggles the color scheme, not on the first load.
Another option is to save `window.scrollY` before `scrollTo(0, 1)` and restore it in the timer, instead of scrolling to 0.

### Your environment

- Safari 27.0 on macOS 27
- Quarto 1.10.18 (repro) and 1.9.32 (docs.posit.co); the same code is on `main`

title: Add an attribute to pass a frame title to `code-preview`
description:
## I have:

- [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues
- [x] installed the latest version of Quarto CLI
- [x] formatted my issue following the Bug Reports guide

## Bug description

The `code-preview` code block attribute adds an iframe that shows the rendered example. Quarto sets only `src` and the classes of the code block, so the iframe has no `title`. An author cannot supply one.

Screen readers announce an iframe by its title, so these frames have no accessible name. axe-core reports this as `frame-title` (serious, WCAG 2.0 A, SC 4.1.2).

The iframe is built in [`src/format/html/format-html.ts#L808-L825`](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/f9dd09cd2aee9f107a6c3f497e9210d55ceeebca/src/format/html/format-html.ts#L808-L825). `data-code-preview` is the only occurrence of the feature in `src/`, and it has no schema entry, so there is no way to set a title.

quarto-web uses `code-preview` 27 times: `docs/presentations/revealjs/index.qmd` (17), `docs/presentations/revealjs/advanced.qmd` (9), and `docs/authoring/code-annotation.qmd` (1). Every one produces an untitled frame.

## Steps to reproduce

Two files in the same directory.

`index.qmd`:

````qmd
---
title: "code-preview iframe"
format: html
---

```{.yaml code-preview="example.qmd"}
format:
  revealjs:
    smaller: true
```
````

`example.qmd`:

````qmd
---
title: "Example"
format: revealjs
---

## A slide
````

Then render both files:

```bash
quarto render example.qmd
quarto render index.qmd
```

## Actual behavior

`index.html` contains an iframe with no `title` attribute:

```html
<iframe class="sourceCode yaml code-with-copy" src="example.html"></iframe>
```

axe-core reports `frame-title` on this page, and no other violation.

## Expected behavior

A `code-preview-title` attribute sets the `title` of the iframe:

````qmd
```{.yaml code-preview="example.qmd" code-preview-title="Example presentation with smaller text"}
format:
  revealjs:
    smaller: true
```
````

The title must come from the author, because no automatic source describes these previews:

- The preview targets carry no `title:` metadata.
- The file name is a topic slug. `examples/smaller.qmd` gives "smaller".
- The first heading can be the counter-example. `examples/smaller.qmd` compares a slide without the class to a slide with it, so it opens with the slide *without* `.smaller`.

Each frame holds a live Reveal.js deck that shows the result of the code block above it. A good title states that relationship, and stays unique on a page that has 17 previews (see the `frame-title-unique` rule).

Writing an accurate title for the 27 previews on quarto.org then becomes a PR on `quarto-web`.
